title: Add KV cache fragmentation ratio + allocation failure metrics (labeled by region/pool/model family)
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Goal
Add production-grade metrics for KV cache fragmentation and allocator failures so we can (a) quantify baseline fragmentation under burst/mixed-length workloads, (b) attribute p95/p99 spikes to allocator churn, and (c) gate compaction canary/rollout.

Scope
1) Fragmentation ratio metric(s)
2) Allocation failure counters
3) Required dimensional labels: region, pool, model_family (plus optional: deployment_mode)
4) Define metric names + units + semantics (so SRE can alert and perf-canary can gate)

Non-goals
- Implementing compaction/eviction behavior (separate tickets)
- Building dashboards/alerts (ENG-2850), but metric design must be compatible

Proposed metrics (naming + semantics)
All metrics should be emitted from serving runtime and ingested via central telemetry.

A. Fragmentation ratio
- Name: runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio
- Type: gauge
- Unit: ratio (0.0–1.0)
- Labels: region, pool, model_family, deployment_mode
- Definition (allocator-level):
  fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (kv_cache_live_blocks / kv_cache_reserved_blocks)
  where:
  - reserved_blocks: total blocks reserved/held by KV cache allocator (including free list / holes)
  - live_blocks: blocks currently mapped to active sequences (in-flight decode/prefill)
  Notes:
  - This intentionally measures “holes” inside the reserved arena, not global GPU free memory.
  - For early rollout, compute at allocator snapshot intervals (not every allocation).

B. Allocation failures
- Name: runtime_kv_cache_allocation_failures_total
- Type: counter
- Unit: failures
- Labels: region, pool, model_family, deployment_mode, failure_reason
- failure_reason values (string enum): oom, arena_exhausted, block_map_full, other
- Semantics:
  - Incremented when allocator cannot satisfy a requested KV block allocation in the fast path.
  - This is distinct from request-level rejection (scheduler admission control). If we can tag those later, do it separately.

C. (Optional but useful for triage) Allocation retry / slow path
- Name: runtime_kv_cache_allocation_slow_path_total
- Type: counter
- Unit: events
- Labels: region, pool, model_family, deployment_mode, slow_path_reason
- slow_path_reason values: free_list_search, compaction_attempted, eviction_attempted
- If this is too much for initial scope, omit and keep a TODO for follow-up.

Implementation notes
- Emission frequency: compute fragmentation ratio on a timer (e.g., 5s) per runtime instance; avoid per-request emission.
- Overhead constraints:
  - No global locks in hot path.
  - Snapshot should use existing allocator counters (atomic) rather than walking block maps.
- Cardinality constraints:
  - model_family should be a coarse string (e.g., llama, qwen, mistral). Avoid full model_id.
  - pool should be normalized to a short stable identifier (e.g., hosted-us-east-1a-gpu-pool-3, dedicated-acct-<hash>-pool-1).
  - deployment_mode values: hosted | dedicated | private
- Logging:
  - On allocation failure, emit a structured log line (rate-limited) including request_id, model_family, requested_blocks, reserved_blocks, live_blocks.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Metrics available in central telemetry within 15 minutes for a canary runtime pod.
- [x] Labels present: region/pool/model_family at minimum; deployment_mode if already available at the emitter.
- [x] Unit tests for fragmentation ratio math and failure_reason mapping.
- [x] No measurable median latency regression in microbench (allocator hot path) from adding counters.
- [x] SRE confirms metric names/units match alerting needs for canary runbook.

Links / references
- Umbrella project: ENG-2841
- Telemetry schema request: INT-1183
- Implementation PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18423.json (KV cache fragmentation metrics + structured logging)
- Runbook/dashboards follow-ups: ENG-2850, ENG-2851

Open questions
1) Do we need tenant_tier as a label for hosted multi-tenant pools? (Concern: cardinality; likely no for v1.)
2) Should fragmentation ratio be computed on blocks or bytes? (Current proposal: blocks; bytes requires more bookkeeping, revisit if needed.)
3) How do we represent “pool” for Dedicated accounts without leaking account identifiers? (Use internal pool slug; no customer names.)
comments: 2025-02-18 (Logan Wright): Creating this as P0 since compaction triggers/rollout gates need a baseline fragmentation signal. Please keep metric label cardinality tight; SRE already flagged high-cardinality issues with model_id tags.

2025-02-19 (Samir Qureshi): Drafted initial metric names. I’m leaning to blocks rather than bytes for the ratio since allocator is block-based already and we can compute without walking segments. Will add a timer-based snapshot so we don’t pay cost per request.

2025-02-20 (Rafael Mendes): For canary we need a hard gate on allocation failures (failures_total > 0 sustained) and a soft signal on fragmentation ratio trending up. Please ensure region/pool labels match what dashboards already use (same pool slug as GPU capacity dashboards).

2025-02-22 (Caleb Johnson): Telemetry pipeline can accept new metrics; please register in schema per INT-1183. For failure_reason, keep values stable (string enum), avoid embedding allocator error text.

2025-02-25 (Samir Qureshi): Implemented allocator counters (reserved_blocks, live_blocks) as atomics updated on map/unmap. Fragmentation ratio computed every 5s; exported via metrics emitter. Allocation failures counter increments on fast-path miss + arena_exhausted return.

2025-02-27 (Logan Wright): PR-18423 looks good. Request: add a unit test for fragmentation ratio bounds (never <0 or >1 even under concurrent updates). Also confirm model_family mapping is coarse (no model_id).

2025-03-01 (Samir Qureshi): Added bounds clamp + tests, and model_family derived from runtime model registry (llama/mistral/qwen/other). Added rate-limited structured log on allocation failure with requested_blocks + snapshot counters.

2025-03-04 (Connor O'Brien): Merged PR-18423 into runtime-1.18 branch. Metrics visible in staging hosted-us-east-1. Marking Done. Follow-ups for alert thresholds/dashboards tracked in ENG-2850/ENG-2851.
